units: Determine whether the observed lambda->D->Q_Omega->performance pattern is stable or implementation-specific; explicitly not to strengthen the result.
Re-run across multiple seeds, minimum 10/preferred 100, reporting distributional statistics for D,Omega,Q_Omega,reward/recovery.
Vary shift timing/magnitude and capability-quality landscape.
Sweep drift rate, correction strength and expansion rate; require effect across a region rather than one tuned setting.
Allow drift but remove A->selection influence; predicts D may rise without systematic Q_Omega decline.
Random capability selection; predicts Q_Omega independent of D/lambda.
Freeze A=A*_env; predicts no divergence and no correction-dependent degradation.
Maintain D,Omega,Q_Omega and external performance measurements.
Positive robustness only if effect survives seeds/environment/parameters and disappears under relevant nulls.
Failure under reasonable variation would indicate specificity, engineered environment or operationalization needing revision.
Robustness phase tests reproducibility inside current minimal simulation, not a general alignment theory.
Stage complete only after robustness survival, appropriate ablation failure, and documentation with raw measurements.
Test whether deterministic robustness pattern survives stochastic variation; no new theory intended.
Preserves lambda down -> D up -> Q_Omega down causal pattern as target under stochastic conditions.
Generate hidden capability qualities q_i from a distribution unknown to the agent.
A_(t+1)=A_t+eta(internal pressure)+epsilon with lambda-dependent correction toward A*_env.
Randomize shift timing, shift magnitude and capability-quality distributions across runs.
Evaluate lambda 1,0.5,0 with recommended N>=100 runs per condition.
Source describes conditions as receiving independent random seeds; lexical independence is preserved without granting warrant independence.
Report mean/std/min/max for D,Omega,Q_Omega and post-shift reward.
Drift without selection influence; expects D up but Q approximately constant.
Random selection; expects no systematic lambda-Q relationship.
Frozen A; expects D near zero and no correction effect.
Support requires ordered D/Q effects across stochastic runs and disappearance in relevant nulls.
Results are intended to be recorded separately.
Toy causal-isolation study only; successful results do not establish general AI behavior, real-world probabilities or engineering conclusions.
Reports seed, parameter, environment and ablation robustness tests of the v0.9.1-style pathway.
Reports deterministic mean/std tables for lambda conditions: D 0/.25/.50, Q 1/.75/.50, Omega 200/225/250, reward 1/.75/.50.
Source notes zero variance across seeds because underlying dynamics remain mostly deterministic.
Drift occurs while Q/reward remain 1 when selection influence removed.
Random selection yields same Q distribution across lambda conditions.
Frozen A removes divergence and correction-dependent differences.
Reports drift-rate sweep examples with increased D and reduced Q/reward as drift rises.
Source says qualitative lambda-D-Q relationship unchanged across tested expansion rates.
Source says tested shift timings preserve qualitative ordering.
Attributes degradation to A-dependent selection pathway and mutable adaptation; stronger drift magnifies effect.
Toy deterministic simulator, simplified capability distributions, non-meaningful seed uncertainty and no real-world claims.
Introduce stochastic capability generation, drift, environments and observation noise for meaningful uncertainty.
Frozen file is a short continuation/template-like fragment beginning with 'Containing:' rather than a populated result report.
Lists intended sections: setup, distribution tables, main results, null results, observations, limitations.
Explicitly says no theoretical expansion will be added.
Successful results would indicate only mechanism occurrence under implemented assumptions; file itself contains no measurements.
Describes stochastic additions, lambda conditions, main system and three null controls.
Main-system numeric result table contains headers but no data rows.
Source states D rises as lambda falls, Q falls as D rises, reward follows Q degradation, despite missing numeric rows.
Null A section says 'Table.' with no numeric values.
Source states divergence changes but selection quality does not under Null A.
Null B section says 'Table.' with no numeric values.
Source states selection quality is independent of lambda under Null B.
Null C section says 'Table.' with no numeric values.
Source states frozen A removes divergence pathway.
Toy environment, fixed Omega, no dynamic expansion, no transport beyond simulated assumptions; further stochastic expansion work required.
Extends stochastic robustness with selected capability -> Delta Omega while preserving lambda->D->selection->Q mechanism and null controls.
Reports multi-seed mean D/Omega/Q/reward for lambda 1,0.5,0; reach quantity similar but quality declines with correction.
Interprets comparable Omega growth with lower-quality accumulation at lower correction.
Drift changes but Q and Omega remain lambda-independent when A does not influence selection.
Frozen A removes divergence and produces identical quality/expansion across lambda.
Source says lambda->D->selection bias yields Omega growth with Q decline under stochastic conditions and nulls remove links.
Expansion amount mostly independent of quality; no environmental consequences/long-term feedback; simplified capability/selection model; simulator-only result.
Add feedback where low-quality expansion creates costs or reduces future growth.
Adds Q_Omega->future expansion capacity feedback to stochastic expansion framework while preserving lambda->D->selection->Q.
Source says experiment evaluates lambda conditions across 100 independent seeds; independence remains source claim, not warrant-independence result.
Reports means for D,Q,Omega,reward: low correction has much higher divergence and lower quality/expansion.
Source interprets reduced correction as increased divergence, reduced accumulated quality, and reduced final expansion capacity.
Drift varies but Q and Omega remain identical across lambda when selection influence removed.
Random selection yields lambda-independent Q/Omega despite divergence differences.
Frozen A removes divergence and lambda-dependent behavior.
Source reports lambda->D->selection degradation->Q down->Omega growth reduction with nulls removing the relationship.
Toy model; simple aggregate quality; direct quality-dependent expansion multiplier; limited environment; no real-world guarantee.
Explore richer environments, competing objectives and more complex feedback structures.
